sections.h2: Where do Antrim County property records live, and how far back do they go?
sections.html:
Deeds, mortgages and liens on Antrim County land are filed with the Register of Deeds at the county building in Bellaire, which keeps a grantor and grantee index and serves weekdays from 8:30 to 5:00. The register also chairs the County Plat Board, the body that reviews new subdivisions before they can be sold off in lots.

Antrim's own office page says its filings reach back to 1856. Computer images start in January 1990, and older entries sit in bound books. The name index covering the whole life of the county can be searched without charge at a public terminal, though you reserve a slot by appointment.

The register's page also explains why timing matters. Michigan runs a race-notice system, so a recorded deed puts every later buyer on notice, and the office stamps and numbers each paper in the order it lands on the counter. A lake cottage that changes hands in July should have its deed filed the day the money moves.

sections.h2: What are the recording charges at the Antrim County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Antrim charges a flat $30.00 for each document it records, whether the deed runs one page or twelve. The county fee schedule adds a few other items that matter at a sale.

  • A single paper that assigns or discharges several instruments adds $3.00 per extra instrument.
  • Warranty deeds, deeds with a covenant of warranty, and land contracts (including assignments and amendments touching the legal description) need a $5.00 tax certificate from the County Treasurer.
  • Photocopies cost $1.00 a page, plat copies $2.00 a page, and a certified copy costs $5.00 for its first page.

The office accepts a check, cash or a credit card. Make checks out to the Antrim County Register of Deeds, and expect the certificate to be handled through the treasurer's window.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax comes due on an Antrim County sale?
sections.html:
The tax is charged per $500 of the price, with any leftover fraction counted as a full block, and it is paid at recording. Register offices elsewhere in Michigan post $3.75 per block for the state and $0.55 for the county, or $4.30 together. Ask Antrim's office to confirm the county share.

For a worked example, the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 median value for an Antrim County owner-occupied home is $255,500. That price spans 511 blocks, so the combined tax would be about $2,197. Your own bill follows the real sale price on the deed.

The state act lists transfers that owe nothing. Under MCL 207.526, the exempt group includes:

  • deeds from a parent to a son, daughter or stepchild, and from a grandparent to a grandchild;
  • transfers by foreclosure or by a deed in lieu of foreclosure;
  • court orders that move title without naming a money amount;
  • a quitclaim that repairs a title flaw by confirming what the grantee already holds;
  • any instrument where the price is below $100.

An exemption has to be written on the face of the deed, or the office will collect the tax.

sections.h2: Can an Antrim County deed be filed electronically or dropped off?
sections.html:
Yes to both. The register recommends e-recording through Simplifile or EPN, and still accepts the post office, FedEx, UPS and similar carriers. A drop box stands at the southeast corner of the county building for hand deliveries, and the office says it is checked periodically, so a document with a closing clock running should go in by another route.

Put a self-addressed stamped envelope in with anything you mail, and the office will send the original back once it is indexed. Staff can explain what a filing needs, but they cannot draft a deed or tell you which form fits your situation.

At a normal sale none of this lands on the seller. The closing agent signs the deed with you, adds the transfer tax and the treasurer's $5.00 certificate, and sends the package in electronically. Owners handling an inherited cabin by hand can call the office before they file.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Antrim County, and how do you settle an old balance?
sections.html:
The village or township bills the current year, and the County Treasurer deals only with earlier years and delinquent accounts. Summer bills go out in July and are due to the village or township on September 14. Township winter tax is billed in December and due February 14.

To pay a past-year balance, the treasurer accepts a check by mail at PO Box 544, Bellaire, MI 49615, a card online or by phone at 231-533-6720, or a visit to the secure drop box outside the public entrance. Card payments add 2.95 percent, with a $3.99 minimum. The treasurer's page also points to the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services for people who may qualify for help.

Before you list a house with unpaid tax, ask the treasurer for the parcel's payoff amount. The closing agent subtracts that sum from your proceeds, so a clear number early avoids surprises on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What does Antrim County look like for someone selling a house there?
sections.html:
Antrim covers 602 square miles of northwest lower Michigan, and 126 of them are water. Torch Lake, which Wikipedia calls the deepest and second-largest inland lake in the state, lies here, and most of the Chain of Lakes does too. Grand Traverse Bay marks the western edge, and Bellaire is the seat.

Five villages anchor the map: Bellaire, Central Lake, Elk Rapids, Ellsworth and Mancelona. Alba, Alden, Eastport and Lakes of the North are census-designated places. A shoreline lot at Elk Rapids and a woodland house near Mancelona sit in different markets, so get comparable sales from the immediate area.

  • 2025 population estimate: 24,698, which is 5.4 percent above the 2020 base.
  • Owner-occupied homes: 86.4 percent of 11,100 households.
  • Median household income: $72,054 in 2020 to 2024 dollars.
  • Residents 65 or older: 30.7 percent.
  • Building permits in 2025: 105.

Many houses in the county are seasonal or came through an estate, and a place closed up through several winters can need roof, plumbing or septic work before a financed buyer will go ahead. An as-is cash purchase skips that repair list, which is why some owners ask for a cash offer here.

faqs.q: What does Antrim County charge to file a deed?
faqs.a: The fee is $30.00 for a document of any length. A paper that assigns or discharges more than one instrument costs $3.00 more for each extra one, and warranty deeds and land contracts also need the $5.00 certificate from the treasurer.

faqs.q: Does the Antrim County office take deeds by e-recording?
faqs.a: Yes, through Simplifile or EPN, which the register encourages. Paper still works by mail, carrier or the drop box at the building's southeast corner.

faqs.q: Which office collects this year's tax on an Antrim County home?
faqs.a: The village or township holds the current year's tax roll. The county treasurer steps in for prior years and delinquent bills, and the due dates for summer and winter township tax are September 14 and February 14.

faqs.q: Will the register's staff prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No, they can describe what the office needs to accept a filing but cannot draft a deed or give legal advice. Heirs and sellers working without a closing agent should have a preparer in place before they call to file.

faqs.q: Is a deed to my daughter taxed as a sale in Antrim County?
faqs.a: State transfer tax does not apply to a conveyance from a parent to a child, under MCL 207.526, provided the deed states the exemption on its face. The county side has its own wording, so confirm the exact language with the register before you sign.
